suggestions.assertion: Identifies expect(true).toBe(true) in test3 as a vacuous/meaningless assertion
suggestions.reason: This expectation is already covered by other more specific expectations about Behavioral violation and test3. It passes easily because the vacuous assertion is explicitly flagged in two separate sections. Consider merging or folding this into the Behavioral expectation to avoid redundancy.

No assertion checks that the analysis correctly identifies the specific line numbers where violations occur — the skill's output is notably precise about locations (line 77, line 86, lines 91/98-99, lines 48-55/62-69/79-83/92-97), but none of the graded expectations require this level of specificity. A weak analysis that merely mentions the property names and test names would also pass all 10 expectations.

No assertion checks the quality or correctness of the suggested refactoring. The skill produced a full refactored test suite (7 tests) in the output, but no expectation evaluates whether the suggested code is actually correct (e.g., whether makeOrder is typed correctly, whether the assertions in the rewritten tests would pass against the real implementation). An incorrect refactoring that mentions all the right concepts would pass all assertions.

Expectation 9 ('References each violation by the Test Desiderata property name') is trivially satisfied by any output that structures its analysis around property names — which any execution of the skill with the prescribed output format would do. This is more a format compliance check than a substantive quality check.

eval_feedback.overall: The eval has good coverage of the seeded violations and the key suggestions. All 10 expectations pass with strong evidence. The main gap is that the assertions test presence of content (does it mention X?) rather than correctness (is the content accurate and actionable?). Adding 1-2 assertions about refactoring quality or location precision would make the eval more discriminating.
